items.title: Guess How Many Deep Sea Animals Are UNKNOWN
items.hook: A one-minute curiosity hit: how much life in the deep ocean have we still never identified?

items.title: GPT-4 predictable scaling: capability from more compute
items.hook: The useful old idea behind today's scaling debates: capability gains could be forecast from smaller training runs before the expensive final run.

items.title: Andrew Ng: skills for using coding agents effectively
items.hook: A compact framework for what humans still need to get good at when coding agents become more autonomous: planning, context, verification and knowing when to intervene.

items.title: How to Prompt Claude 5: 7 Essential Rules from Anthropic
items.hook: Less step-by-step micromanagement, more delegation: give the whole job, context, guardrails and a crisp definition of done.

items.title: The paradox at the heart of AI and science | Terence Tao
items.hook: AI can get you to the answer faster while quietly stealing the wrong turns that build understanding. Tao's helicopter-vs-hike metaphor is worth sitting with.

items.title: Don't Ship Skills Without Evals — Philipp Schmid
items.hook: Almost exactly the experiment you need for reusable agent skills: ablate the skill, isolate runs, measure it, and delete it when the base model catches up.

items.title: The First Nuclear Space Ship
items.hook: A fast detour from AI: why nuclear power could change what spacecraft can do far from Earth.

items.title: Stanford CS153 Frontier Systems | Scale, AGI, and the Future of Everything
items.hook: The most relevant part isn't AGI speculation: it's the question of which thinking, writing, coding and verification muscles we should deliberately keep exercising when AI can do the task.

items.title: Star Trek: The Original Series - Season One - re:View
items.hook: Not everything here needs to improve your career. A long-form Star Trek season-one discussion for when entertainment is exactly what you want.

items.title: Why The Harness Matters More Than The Model | YC Paper Club
items.hook: The deep version of a theme you've been circling: reliable agents emerge from state, context, tools, memory and control loops—not just a smarter model.

items.title: Elon Musk & Gwynne Shotwell on AI Risks, Starship and Terafab
items.hook: A broader industrial/space conversation, with one particularly interesting idea: rival AI labs adversarially testing each other's models before release.

items.title: Azure agents framework
items.hook: A real course rather than a snack. Keep it for a deliberate learning block: Agent Framework, MCP, workflows, multi-agent orchestration and A2A are the high-value sections.
